compare_blocks.body:
The fictional scenes concern how relatives share information. The treating team explains clinical questions, while the hospital’s billing team and the insurer explain costs, coverage and refunds. In an emergency, call the local emergency number and follow the dispatcher’s instructions.

The relatives can agree who will verify the bill and who will update the family. Either can do both, depending on access to the records and availability.

### ENFJ and INTP: the deposit — who speaks and who reconciles, decided by conditions

(Fictional scene) The division is not made by type: whoever holds the paperwork checks the receipts and the reimbursement rules; whoever can reach people makes the calls; whoever is free that day goes to the window. One person can take both segments, as long as both are written on the same sheet so nothing is missed.

In this fictional example, either relative can discuss how a request for help would affect the household and verify the dates, amounts and assumptions in the estimate. The same person can raise both concerns.

Draw one line: how much each family member contributes and how it is recorded is for the two of them to decide; what insurance covers, how much, and how much of the deposit comes back is whatever the settlement desk and the insurance office say. Neither needs to judge on the other's behalf what this illness will cost — that belongs to the doctor and the billing department.

Afterwards, keep a record that does not type anyone: each writes one sentence on when this money gets back to the other person, and one on what the other person cares about most. Only with both is the matter properly closed. Whether the date or the human side comes more easily is a trace of habit and of the role held at the time, not evidence of type.

### ENFJ and INTP: asking the uncle — whether to borrow, and how to say it

(Fictional scene) The deposit is three thousand short, and the uncle is the most likely source of help. One consideration starts with what three thousand means in his household — whether his wife knows, whether it will cause a row, whether to borrow a little less; the other starts with how to state the conditions — when it will be repaid, how, and whether to write a note. Both are asking about two sides of one thing: once the money goes out, the relationship and the account both have to land somewhere. Either consideration can come from the same person, and the order shifts with conditions.

Each emphasis can go wrong. Attending only to the relationship may get the money and put the uncle in a difficult position when his wife later finds out; attending only to conditions may sound like a contract and make him feel kept at arm's length. The reverse happens too: an INTP will sometimes deliberately not mention repayment for fear of seeming distant; an ENFJ will sometimes offer to write a note, worried the other will not feel able to ask.

So before speaking, each writes one sentence that the other must know, and after swapping, each adds one more. Whether the sentence is a date or a difficulty reflects what mattered more at the time, not who understands people better.

If the aunt later asks when the money can be repaid, the one who can answer is usually the one who kept the record — a result of the division of work, not of type.
compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
The first misread is that ENFJ only works relationships and cannot handle accounts. Raising money involves arithmetic, and anyone who has done it for years will work out interest and dates as a matter of course; that is experience, not preference.

The second is that INTP is cold and does not care. Doing the arithmetic first often happens because only a clear figure makes the help possible; "do not let the parents worry" has been translated into "have the plan ready".

The third comes from "only two functions are shared, so the difference must be large". Which two are shared, and in which two seats they sit, is a way of describing the model and does not measure how different two people are. In the writing used here, Fe and Ti exchange between dominant and inferior; that says where the emphasis lands, not who is stronger or harder to get along with, and it is not evidence about the size of a real difference.

The fourth treats J as more decisive. An ENFJ will also keep asking people when information is thin, and an INTP will also settle something in one sentence once the figures are clear.

The fifth uses who phones first as a test. With the same deposit, whether to speak first or calculate first depends on duty, deadline, experience and how many people are present; recording the order as evidence of type stops working the moment the post changes.

The attitude of the third process is labelled differently elsewhere — check the source when versions disagree, then read the pair through the first two positions.
items.question: The stacks share only two functions — what does that show?

items.answer:
Not by frequency and not by order, but by which kind of evidence is taken first across comparable situations.

A usable question looks back at the reason: do you more often stop because of how the other person will feel and who is affected, or because the date, the amount and the rule do not reconcile. Both types do the other thing; the difference is which side gets taken first.
items.question: An INTP also asks for help, an ENFJ also reconciles the accounts — how do you tell them apart?

items.answer:
Divide by who holds the paperwork, who can reach people and who is free that day — not by type.

A usable agreement reconciles once a day: how much was borrowed, how much repaid, how much still short — five minutes is enough. The specific rules on reimbursement and deposits are whatever the settlement desk and the insurance office say; do not substitute a guess.
items.question: How should the two cooperate on raising money and filing paperwork?

items.answer:
In the fictional conversation about borrowing, either relative can consider how the request could affect the family relationship and whether the proposed terms are clear and practical.

Both can work, and both can wound. The steadier approach does both — warm words and a clear note, ideally with the date read aloud in front of both households. Who writes the note and who speaks follows who is present and who knows the other better at the time.
items.question: Lending between relatives — where do the two differ?

items.answer:
Check first whether it was the same tool, the same version and the same scoring definition; under different definitions, two sets of labels cannot be compared directly.

If it was the same tool and it reports dimension results, check E/I, T/F and J/P separately rather than looking at only two of them. The situation while answering changes self-description — a period spent mainly as the outward contact, for instance — but two labels alone cannot establish the cause of the change, whether it was a measurement error, or which sitting is closer to you.

sections.body_md:
Framework sources: definitions of the four preference pairs follow the [Myers-Briggs official facts page](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts); the type-dynamics framework follows the [Foundation's note on type dynamics](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-processes/) and the [type dynamics overview](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/).

Four-position convention on this page: Fe–Ni–Se–Ti for ENFJ and Ti–Ne–Si–Fe for INTP follow one common four-position notation adopted here as an editorial convention; the attitude of the third process is not labelled uniformly across sources, and this page uses the common writing without presenting it as the Foundation's only reading. The Foundation material is used to explain preferences and type dynamics, not to replace the specific markings here.

Editorial fiction note: the hospital deposit and the request to the uncle are editorial fiction, corresponding to no real person or event, used to illustrate how people can weigh the same information, and constituting no medical or financial advice. Judgements about the condition and the settlement of costs belong to the attending doctor, the hospital settlement desk and the insurance office.

Scope limits: the comparison here describes emphasis inside the model; it does not predict the order of behaviour, does not measure levels of ability, and is not for hiring screens or predicting relationships.
